page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, translating to 4.0 GB of memory per core. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance utilizes a dedicated Intel processor with 1 physical core and 2 threads per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance achieves average tier performance in single-core metrics, such as a stress-ng single-core score of 1684.29 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1834.0. However, multi-core and memory-intensive operations show significant limitations. The stress-ng multi-core performance of 1714.68 and PassMark CPU score of 2984.94 are categorized in the bottom 10%, reflecting the constraints of having only a single physical core. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block bandwidth at 19.35 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 12.78 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 10% tier.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, the n4-standard-2 is positioned as an entry-level general-purpose option. It is suitable for lightweight, single-threaded tasks such as basic text processing, simple web serving, or small-scale development environments where multi-core throughput is not critical. It exhibits weak performance in database operations and software compilation, making it less suitable for heavy production databases or CI/CD pipelines. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, it offers a low-cost entry point to dedicated Intel hardware, but users face a steep performance tradeoff for multi-threaded or memory-bound workloads.
